marble.name: Comparing Large Numbers
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.prompt: Can you put a set of four-digit numbers like 4,321, 1,876, and 9,045 in order from smallest to largest — comparing them digit by digit?

cluster.summary: Your child is building number foundations — learning to read and write numbers up to 100, understanding number words, and beginning to see how numbers are built from tens and ones.

misconceptions: Comparing by number of digits incorrectly, or by the largest single digit.
Not descending to the next place on a tie (declaring equal too early).
Aligning numbers to the left instead of by place value (mixed lengths).
Reversing the symbol or binding it to reading order.
representations: Aligned numerals / place-value charts stacked by place
Real-context data (populations, distances) as numbers to order
authoredAnswer: 3,472 > 3,427; order 8,091 < 8,901 < 8,910; comparing from the highest place value down.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: 3,472 vs 3,427 is judged by the ones (2 vs 7), rather than the first differing place, the tens (7 vs 2); thousands and hundreds tie.
wrongAnswers.fix: Right-align the numbers in place-value columns and compare from the leftmost place, stopping at the first place that differs.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: A shorter number is called larger, or numbers aren't lined up by place before comparing.
wrongAnswers.fix: Line numbers up by columns; a number reaching a higher place (thousands) beats one that doesn't. Contrast 999 and 1,001.
